correctness.rationale: A coordinate in the ternary field has square one precisely when it is nonzero. The idempotent vector is uniquely reconstructed from its support via matrix row sums, yielding seven exact support tests. A complete 19,683-matrix enumeration uses exact determinant and reachability tests, independently cross-checked by Gaussian rank, direct enumeration of all 27 vectors, and BFS connectivity. Monomial basis-change group has exactly 48 elements. Class counts were independently reproduced by stabilizer/Burnside weighting and complete orbit partitioning. All numerical assertions and witnesses were executed in census.py with VERIFY_OK; sums are 11232 and 249, the first moment is exactly 11232. The statements are only finite, with no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the full exact distribution by number of nonzero idempotents of ternary three-dimensional perfect evolution algebras, including simple and isomorphism-class strata. Prior Wei–Zou counts only aggregate isomorphism classes and is cited explicitly for 249; the 2026 survey provides mean-one and asymptotic conjectures, and Hu studies complex full-support solvability. Actual published-finding corpus and public-literature query comparisons found no statement or implication covering the refined four histograms. Earlier unindexed or implicit formulas remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The first nonbinary field and the three-dimensional case form a natural exact benchmark for a 2026 explicit random-idempotent distribution question. The joint four-way stratification discovers a forbidden count 6 among perfect algebras and a sharp at-most-3 bound among simple ones, with 3408 of 7504 simple labeled matrices idempotent-free. The class-level breakdown distinguishes intrinsic algebra types from label multiplicities and can benchmark future asymptotic or representation results. A complete natural finite classification is substantively motivated even without a general theorem.
